name: Kolvex FilterMask FM-12 Urban Half-Face
description: A matte charcoal thermoplastic half-face mask covering nose to chin, manufactured by Kolvex with the same utilitarian honesty as their transit-grade filtration caps. The mask body has a slight anatomical curve and sits flush against the face via a dual-strap silicone seal. Two replaceable hex-cartridge filters flank the exhalation valve — cartridges are color-coded: grey for particulate, amber for chemical, red for biological. The exterior is stamped with the Kolvex hexagon mark in debossed relief.
functionality: Filters PM2.5 particulate, low-concentration industrial solvents, and common urban aerosols. Cartridges rated for 80 hours of use. Strap system adjusts for most head sizes including those with neck-level chrome augmentation.
what_it_says: You take the air quality seriously but you're not trying to make a statement about it.
worn_by: small business owners near industrial zones
manufacturer: Kolvex (corponation, transit and safety equipment division)
story_hooks: A batch of FM-12s sold in Circuit Ward 7 had amber cartridges that tested positive for a rare neurotoxin — whether contamination or sabotage is unresolved.
The silicone seal leaves a faint ring on the face after long wear — a visible mark that Circuit workers recognize and Spire residents find unsettling.
Someone has been swapping used red bio-cartridges back into sealed packaging and reselling them; the next outbreak could trace back to a single counterfeit shipment.
